A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AliTok research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across additions, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: V2 reports original ImageNet generation and reconstruction results, component ablations, training curves, attention analyses, and sampling measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds ImageNet-512 experiments, larger-codebook results, efficiency analyses, and qualitative text-to-image experiments.

M1.justification: The core tokenizer architecture, losses, prefix-token design, and two-stage procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A.4 adds a LLaVA-OV-0.5B-based unified text/image autoregressive model incorporating AliTok, providing a limited model adaptation beyond the original class-conditional generator.

E1.justification: V3 extends ImageNet generation from 256×256 to 512×512 and adds CC12M training with qualitative text-to-image evaluation at 512×512. This substantially broadens resolution, represented data, and conditioning requirements beyond v2's ImageNet class-conditional experiments.

E2.justification: The original comparison tables retain their comparator sets. V3 adds TiTok-L-32 to the supplementary reconstruction comparison and Janus-pro-1B to the new qualitative text-to-image comparison. REPA and MAR-L in the new ImageNet-512 table were already evaluated at 256 resolution in v2.

E3.justification: Added protocols include fine-tuning the tokenizer and generator from 256 to 512 resolution with tokenizer embedding interpolation, comparing 4,096 and 16,384 codebooks at 400 AR epochs, and evaluating reconstruction with PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS. V3 also introduces cache-on/off and resolution-dependent resource controls, plus 30,000-step multimodal training. The original ImageNet-256 protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and attention analyses, v3 tests vocabulary-size sensitivity, isolates KV-caching's contribution to sampling speed, measures prefix-token overhead across resolutions, and examines classwise codebook geometry using t-SNE. These add substantial evidence addressing scalability and mechanism questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The new results continue the existing practice of reporting point estimates and qualitative visualizations.

E6.justification: Original ImageNet-256 results are retained. New results include AliTok-L's ImageNet-512 gFID 1.39 and IS 295.3 (Table 5), the 16,384-codebook variant's rFID 0.81 and gFID 1.30 versus 0.86 and 1.28 for 4,096 (Table 6), and sampling times of 107.76 versus 10.07 seconds without/with caching (Table 11). V3 also adds reconstruction metrics, overhead measurements, t-SNE findings, and text-to-image examples.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), mathematical definitions, and causal reconstruction formulation are retained. The new prefix-scaling discussion explains the existing W versus H×W token counts; it does not introduce a substantive new formal result, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract adds a state-of-the-art ImageNet-512 claim for the 318M model at gFID 1.39. The central alignment contribution, ImageNet-256 performance claims, sampling-speed claim, and conclusion otherwise retain their meaning.

C2.justification: V2 leaves larger-codebook exploration to future work; v3 interprets the tested vocabulary expansion as introducing a learning difficulty that may require longer training or larger models. Appendix A.4 additionally attributes improved learnability to semantic disentanglement in t-SNE, explains declining relative prefix overhead, and discusses preliminary multimodal applicability. These substantially expand the mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Table 8 newly documents tokenizer codebook dimensions, parameter counts, batch size, learning-rate bounds, and training epochs. V3 also supplies embedding-interpolation details and the multimodal backbone, training steps, and 64-A100 hardware configuration. These extend documentation; the original sampling hyperparameters and code/weights access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for CC12M, LLaVA-OneVision, FACM, DreamVideo, and diffusion-transformer routing, while removing the GPT-4o system card and Emu3 references. Janus-pro gains an experimental comparison role. The main positioning around aligning tokenization with standard autoregressive modeling remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. V3 updates the abstract, author-role and conference-header text, revises the limitations paragraph, adds acknowledgments, and inserts experimental subsections. The additions do not constitute an extensive rewrite of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: V3 adds six tables covering new experiments and specifications, plus figures for ImageNet-512 samples, t-SNE, and text-to-image comparisons. Existing displays are retained: v2 Table 5 becomes Table 7, Table 6 becomes Table 9, and the original sample galleries move to Figures 14–18. The added displays substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens practical validation through the previously untested larger-codebook experiment, ImageNet-512 results, and controlled cache/overhead measurements. Tokenizer training disclosures also improve reproducibility. However, the t-SNE plots provide limited support for the stronger mechanism interpretations, and the text-to-image comparison uses only qualitative examples with unequal model sizes and training budgets. The net gain is useful but bounded.
